title: Neural Architecture Search (NAS)
description: NAS: Automate neural network architecture design. Search space, search strategy, performance estimation. DARTS, EfficientNet, AutoML. Hardware-aware NAS.

content.level0_basic: Neural Architecture Search (NAS): Automatically design optimal neural network architecture (layers, connections, hyperparameters). Manual design (ResNet, VGG) → AutoML. Components: (1) Search space (possible architectures), (2) Search strategy (how to explore: RL, evolution, gradient-based), (3) Performance estimation (train & evaluate). Example: Google AutoML designed EfficientNet (SOTA ImageNet), NASNet. Benefits: Better accuracy (SOTA), faster (hardware-aware), democratize (non-experts). Cost: Expensive (thousands of GPU hours), but one-shot methods reduce.
content.level1_beginner: Search strategies: (1) Reinforcement Learning (NASNet, controller RNN predicts architecture, reward = accuracy), (2) Evolutionary (population of architectures, mutate, crossover, select), (3) Gradient-based (DARTS: differentiable, continuous relaxation, backprop through architecture), (4) One-shot (train supernet, weight sharing, architecture sampling). Search spaces: (1) Cell-based (search micro-architecture cell, stack), (2) Macro (full network), (3) Hierarchical. Performance estimation: (1) Full training (expensive), (2) Early stopping (proxy), (3) Weight sharing (one-shot), (4) Zero-cost proxies (no training). Frameworks: NAS-Bench, AutoKeras, Auto-PyTorch, Google Cloud AutoML.
content.level2_application: Applications: (1) Computer Vision (EfficientNet, NASNet, object detection), (2) NLP (Evolved Transformer, architecture search for BERT), (3) Time series (AutoTS), (4) Recommendation (AutoRec). Hardware-aware NAS: Optimize for latency, memory, energy (mobile, edge). Multi-objective: Accuracy + efficiency (Pareto frontier). Deployment: Once architecture found → train from scratch (full epochs), deploy. Cost reduction: One-shot (DARTS, ENAS), weight sharing (hours vs weeks). Cloud NAS: Google Cloud AutoML, Azure AutoML, AWS SageMaker Autopilot.
content.level3_advanced: Advanced: (1) DARTS (Differentiable Architecture Search, continuous relaxation, first-order/second-order), (2) EfficientNet (compound scaling: width, depth, resolution), (3) ProxylessNAS (hardware-aware, mobile latency), (4) Once-for-All (train once, deploy many, elastic depth/width/resolution), (5) NAS-Bench (benchmark datasets, reproducibility), (6) Zero-cost NAS (no training, SNIP, GraSP, NWOT). Challenges: Search cost (GPU hours), transferability (different tasks/datasets), fairness (search space bias), interpretability (black box).
content.level4_expert: Production: Search space design (domain knowledge), multi-fidelity optimization (early stopping, low-resolution proxy), ensemble (multiple architectures), continual NAS (evolving architecture), privacy-preserving NAS (federated NAS). Research: Lifelong NAS (task sequence), neural architecture optimization (beyond search), theoretical foundations (expressivity, generalization), quantum NAS, neuro-symbolic NAS. Benchmarks: NAS-Bench-101/201/301, TransNAS-Bench. Open problems: Generalization to new domains, search cost reduction, interpretability, fairness.

whatIsIt: Neural Architecture Search (NAS): Core concept with mathematical formulation.
whyNeeded: Neural Architecture Search (NAS) addresses critical challenges in modern ML systems.
realWorldAnalogy: Neural Architecture Search (NAS) explained through intuitive real-world analogy.

formulas: \text{Search Cost}: \quad \text{Cost} = |\text{Search Space}| \times \text{Training Time} \quad \text{(naive, billions of GPU hours)}

stepByStep: 1. **Define Search Space**: Cell-based (normal cell + reduction cell) veya chain-structured (sequence of layers). Operations: conv3x3, conv5x5, maxpool, skip-connection, dilated conv. Topology: DAG (directed acyclic graph), N nodes, edge = operation

2. **Initialize Supernet (One-Shot)**: Tüm olası operation'ları içeren over-parameterized network. Architecture parameters α (edge weights), network weights w. Mixed operation: o_bar(x) = Σ softmax(α_i) * op_i(x)

3. **Bi-Level Optimization (DARTS)**: (a) Train weights w: minimize L_train(w,α), SGD on training set. (b) Update architecture α: minimize L_val(w*(α),α), gradient descent on validation set. Alternate between w and α updates
4. **Architecture Derivation**: α converged → Discrete architecture. Her edge için en yüksek softmax(α_i)'ye sahip operation'ı seç: o* = argmax_i α_i. Prune weak edges (threshold)
5. **Retrain from Scratch**: Bulunan architecture ile full training (daha fazla epoch, data augmentation, regularization). One-shot training weights typically discard → fresh init better performance
6. **Evaluate & Deploy**: Final accuracy, latency, FLOPs ölç. Hardware-aware NAS: Latency constraint'i ekle: L_total = L_acc + λ·L_latency. Pareto frontier: accuracy-efficiency tradeoff
algorithm.complexity: Naive NAS: O(|S|·T) (|S|=search space size 10^18, T=training time → infeasible). DARTS (one-shot): O(|O|·T) (|O|=operations ~8, single supernet training). Evolutionary: O(P·G·T) (P=population size, G=generations). RL-based: O(K·T) (K=sampled architectures). Memory: DARTS O(|E|·|O|) (E edges, O operations, store all operation weights). Hardware-aware: +O(L) latency measurement per architecture.

codeExamples.title: DARTS (Differentiable Architecture Search) Core
codeExamples.code:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

class MixedOp(nn.Module):
    """Mixed operation: weighted sum of candidate operations"""
    def __init__(self, C_in, C_out, stride=1):
        super().__init__()
        self.ops = nn.ModuleList([
            nn.Conv2d(C_in, C_out, 3, stride, 1),  # conv3x3
            nn.Conv2d(C_in, C_out, 5, stride, 2),  # conv5x5
            nn.MaxPool2d(3, stride, 1),            # maxpool
            nn.Identity() if stride == 1 else nn.AvgPool2d(2),  # skip
            nn.Conv2d(C_in, C_out, 3, stride, 2, dilation=2),  # dilated conv
        ])
    
    def forward(self, x, weights):
        """Forward: ō(x) = Σ softmax(α_i) * op_i(x)"""
        return sum(w * op(x) for w, op in zip(F.softmax(weights, dim=0), self.ops))

class DARTSCell(nn.Module):
    """NAS cell: 4 nodes (2 inputs, 2 intermediate, 1 output)"""
    def __init__(self, C, n_nodes=4, n_ops=5):
        super().__init__()
        self.n_nodes = n_nodes
        
        # Mixed operations for each edge (i,j) where i < j
        self.edges = nn.ModuleList()
        for i in range(n_nodes):
            for j in range(i+1, n_nodes):
                self.edges.append(MixedOp(C, C))
    
    def forward(self, x, arch_weights):
        """DAG forward: each node = sum of incoming edges"""
        states = [x, x]  # Initial 2 input nodes
        offset = 0
        
        for j in range(2, self.n_nodes):
            # Node j aggregates from all previous nodes i < j
            node_output = []
            for i in range(j):
                edge_idx = offset + i
                node_output.append(self.edges[edge_idx](states[i], arch_weights[edge_idx]))
            states.append(sum(node_output))  # Aggregate
            offset += j
        
        # Concatenate intermediate nodes as output
        return torch.cat(states[2:], dim=1)

class DARTSNetwork(nn.Module):
    """Supernet: stack of NAS cells with architecture parameters"""
    def __init__(self, C=16, n_cells=8, n_classes=10):
        super().__init__()
        self.cells = nn.ModuleList([DARTSCell(C) for _ in range(n_cells)])
        self.classifier = nn.Linear(C * (n_cells * 2), n_classes)  # Assuming 2 intermediate nodes per cell
        
        # Architecture parameters (learnable!)
        n_edges = 6  # For 4 nodes: (0,1), (0,2), (1,2), (0,3), (1,3), (2,3)
        n_ops = 5
        self.arch_params = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(n_edges, n_ops) * 1e-3)
    
    def forward(self, x):
        for cell in self.cells:
            x = cell(x, self.arch_params)
        x = F.adaptive_avg_pool2d(x, 1).flatten(1)
        return self.classifier(x)
    
    def derive_architecture(self):
        """Discretize: select best operation per edge"""
        gene = []
        for edge_weights in self.arch_params:
            best_op_idx = edge_weights.argmax().item()
            op_names = ['conv3x3', 'conv5x5', 'maxpool', 'skip', 'dilated']
            gene.append(op_names[best_op_idx])
        return gene

# DARTS training: Bi-level optimization
model = DARTSNetwork(C=16, n_cells=8, n_classes=10)
optim_w = torch.optim.SGD(model.parameters(), lr=0.025, momentum=0.9)  # Network weights
optim_a = torch.optim.Adam([model.arch_params], lr=3e-4)  # Architecture params

for epoch in range(50):
    # Phase 1: Update weights w on training set
    for X_train, y_train in train_loader:
        optim_w.zero_grad()
        loss_train = F.cross_entropy(model(X_train), y_train)
        loss_train.backward()
        optim_w.step()
    
    # Phase 2: Update architecture α on validation set
    for X_val, y_val in val_loader:
        optim_a.zero_grad()
        loss_val = F.cross_entropy(model(X_val), y_val)
        loss_val.backward()
        optim_a.step()
    
    if epoch % 10 == 0:
        print(f"Epoch {epoch}: Val loss = {loss_val.item():.3f}")
        print(f"Current architecture: {model.derive_architecture()}")

# Final architecture
final_arch = model.derive_architecture()
print(f"\nDiscovered architecture: {final_arch}")
print("Now retrain from scratch with this architecture for best performance!")
codeExamples.explanation: DARTS (Differentiable Architecture Search): Continuous relaxation ile architecture search'ü differentiable yapar → gradient descent! Mixed operation: Her edge, tüm olası operation'ların weighted sum'ı (weight = softmax(α)). Bi-level optimization: (1) Train set'te weight w'yi güncelle, (2) Val set'te architecture α'yı güncelle. Search space: Cell-based (micro-architecture), 10^18 discrete → continuous. Converge sonrası: argmax(α) ile discrete architecture derive et, retrain from scratch.

codeExamples.title: Evolutionary Neural Architecture Search
codeExamples.code:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import numpy as np
import random
from copy import deepcopy

class EvolutionaryNAS:
    """Evolutionary algorithm: mutation + crossover + selection"""
    def __init__(self, population_size=50, generations=30, mutation_rate=0.2):
        self.population_size = population_size
        self.generations = generations
        self.mutation_rate = mutation_rate
        self.search_space = {
            'n_layers': [3, 5, 7, 10],
            'filters': [16, 32, 64, 128, 256],
            'kernel_sizes': [3, 5, 7],
            'pool_types': ['max', 'avg', 'none'],
            'activations': ['relu', 'leaky_relu', 'elu']
        }
    
    def random_architecture(self):
        """Generate random CNN architecture (genome)"""
        n_layers = random.choice(self.search_space['n_layers'])
        genome = []
        for _ in range(n_layers):
            gene = {
                'filters': random.choice(self.search_space['filters']),
                'kernel': random.choice(self.search_space['kernel_sizes']),
                'pool': random.choice(self.search_space['pool_types']),
                'activation': random.choice(self.search_space['activations'])
            }
            genome.append(gene)
        return genome
    
    def mutate(self, genome):
        """Mutation: randomly change one gene"""
        if random.random() < self.mutation_rate:
            mutated = deepcopy(genome)
            if random.random() < 0.5 and len(mutated) > 1:
                # Remove layer
                mutated.pop(random.randint(0, len(mutated)-1))
            else:
                # Add layer
                mutated.insert(random.randint(0, len(mutated)), {
                    'filters': random.choice(self.search_space['filters']),
                    'kernel': random.choice(self.search_space['kernel_sizes']),
                    'pool': random.choice(self.search_space['pool_types']),
                    'activation': random.choice(self.search_space['activations'])
                })
            return mutated
        return genome
    
    def crossover(self, parent1, parent2):
        """Crossover: combine two parent genomes"""
        cutpoint = random.randint(1, min(len(parent1), len(parent2)) - 1)
        child1 = parent1[:cutpoint] + parent2[cutpoint:]
        child2 = parent2[:cutpoint] + parent1[cutpoint:]
        return child1, child2
    
    def evaluate_fitness(self, genome, train_loader, val_loader, epochs=5):
        """Build and train model from genome, return val accuracy"""
        model = self.build_model(genome, n_classes=10)
        optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=0.001)
        
        # Quick training (fitness proxy)
        model.train()
        for epoch in range(epochs):
            for X, y in train_loader:
                optimizer.zero_grad()
                loss = nn.functional.cross_entropy(model(X), y)
                loss.backward()
                optimizer.step()
        
        # Evaluate fitness (validation accuracy)
        model.eval()
        correct = 0
        total = 0
        with torch.no_grad():
            for X, y in val_loader:
                pred = model(X).argmax(1)
                correct += (pred == y).sum().item()
                total += len(y)
        
        fitness = correct / total
        return fitness
    
    def build_model(self, genome, n_classes=10):
        """Build PyTorch model from genome"""
        layers = []
        in_channels = 3
        for gene in genome:
            layers.append(nn.Conv2d(in_channels, gene['filters'], gene['kernel'], padding=gene['kernel']//2))
            if gene['activation'] == 'relu':
                layers.append(nn.ReLU())
            elif gene['activation'] == 'leaky_relu':
                layers.append(nn.LeakyReLU())
            elif gene['activation'] == 'elu':
                layers.append(nn.ELU())
            
            if gene['pool'] == 'max':
                layers.append(nn.MaxPool2d(2))
            elif gene['pool'] == 'avg':
                layers.append(nn.AvgPool2d(2))
            
            in_channels = gene['filters']
        
        layers.extend([nn.AdaptiveAvgPool2d(1), nn.Flatten(), nn.Linear(in_channels, n_classes)])
        return nn.Sequential(*layers)
    
    def evolve(self, train_loader, val_loader):
        """Evolutionary search: mutation + crossover + selection"""
        # Initialize population
        population = [self.random_architecture() for _ in range(self.population_size)]
        
        for gen in range(self.generations):
            print(f"\n=== Generation {gen+1}/{self.generations} ===")
            
            # Evaluate fitness
            fitness_scores = [(genome, self.evaluate_fitness(genome, train_loader, val_loader)) 
                              for genome in population]
            fitness_scores.sort(key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
            
            print(f"Best fitness: {fitness_scores[0][1]:.3f}, Worst: {fitness_scores[-1][1]:.3f}")
            print(f"Best genome layers: {len(fitness_scores[0][0])}")
            
            # Selection: keep top 50%
            survivors = [genome for genome, _ in fitness_scores[:self.population_size//2]]
            
            # Crossover + Mutation: generate offspring
            offspring = []
            while len(offspring) < self.population_size - len(survivors):
                parent1, parent2 = random.sample(survivors, 2)
                child1, child2 = self.crossover(parent1, parent2)
                offspring.extend([self.mutate(child1), self.mutate(child2)])
            
            # New population
            population = survivors + offspring[:self.population_size - len(survivors)]
        
        # Return best architecture
        final_fitness = [(g, self.evaluate_fitness(g, train_loader, val_loader, epochs=10)) for g in population]
        best_genome, best_fitness = max(final_fitness, key=lambda x: x[1])
        return best_genome, best_fitness

# Run evolutionary NAS
nas = EvolutionaryNAS(population_size=20, generations=10)
best_architecture, best_acc = nas.evolve(train_loader, val_loader)

print(f"\n🏆 Best discovered architecture (Val Acc: {best_acc:.2%}):")
for i, layer in enumerate(best_architecture):
    print(f"  Layer {i+1}: {layer['filters']} filters, {layer['kernel']}x{layer['kernel']} kernel, "
          f"{layer['pool']} pool, {layer['activation']}")
codeExamples.explanation: Evolutionary NAS: Doğal seçilim ilhamı. Population of architectures → Mutate (random layer add/remove/change) + Crossover (combine 2 parents) → Select fittest (highest val accuracy) → Repeat.장점: Search space flexible, parallelizable (evaluate population in parallel). 단점: Computationally expensive (train each candidate), no gradient info. Real-world: Google Brain'in NASNet (2017), AmoebaNet. Production: Use surrogate models (predict fitness without training), early stopping (5 epochs proxy), weight sharing.

codeExamples.title: Hardware-Aware NAS (Latency-Constrained)
codeExamples.code:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import time

class HardwareAwareNAS:
    """Optimize for accuracy AND latency (mobile deployment)"""
    def __init__(self, target_latency_ms=50, lambda_latency=0.1):
        self.target_latency = target_latency_ms / 1000  # Convert to seconds
        self.lambda_latency = lambda_latency  # Tradeoff weight
    
    def measure_latency(self, model, input_size=(1, 3, 224, 224), n_runs=100):
        """Measure inference latency on target device (CPU/GPU/mobile)"""
        model.eval()
        dummy_input = torch.randn(input_size)
        
        # Warmup
        with torch.no_grad():
            for _ in range(10):
                _ = model(dummy_input)
        
        # Measure
        torch.cuda.synchronize() if torch.cuda.is_available() else None
        start = time.time()
        with torch.no_grad():
            for _ in range(n_runs):
                _ = model(dummy_input)
        torch.cuda.synchronize() if torch.cuda.is_available() else None
        end = time.time()
        
        latency = (end - start) / n_runs
        return latency * 1000  # Convert to ms
    
    def multi_objective_fitness(self, model, val_loader, input_size):
        """Fitness = accuracy - λ * latency_penalty"""
        # Accuracy
        model.eval()
        correct = 0
        total = 0
        with torch.no_grad():
            for X, y in val_loader:
                pred = model(X).argmax(1)
                correct += (pred == y).sum().item()
                total += len(y)
        accuracy = correct / total
        
        # Latency
        latency_ms = self.measure_latency(model, input_size)
        latency_penalty = max(0, latency_ms - self.target_latency * 1000)  # Penalty if exceed target
        
        # Combined objective
        fitness = accuracy - self.lambda_latency * latency_penalty
        
        print(f"  Accuracy: {accuracy:.3f}, Latency: {latency_ms:.1f}ms, Fitness: {fitness:.3f}")
        return fitness, accuracy, latency_ms
    
    def efficient_block(self, C_in, C_out, expansion=4, use_se=False):
        """MobileNetV3-style inverted residual block"""
        hidden_dim = C_in * expansion
        layers = [
            # Expansion (1x1 conv)
            nn.Conv2d(C_in, hidden_dim, 1, bias=False),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(hidden_dim),
            nn.ReLU6(inplace=True),
            # Depthwise (3x3 conv, groups=channels)
            nn.Conv2d(hidden_dim, hidden_dim, 3, padding=1, groups=hidden_dim, bias=False),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(hidden_dim),
            nn.ReLU6(inplace=True),
        ]
        
        # Squeeze-and-Excitation (optional)
        if use_se:
            layers.extend([
                nn.AdaptiveAvgPool2d(1),
                nn.Conv2d(hidden_dim, hidden_dim // 4, 1),
                nn.ReLU(inplace=True),
                nn.Conv2d(hidden_dim // 4, hidden_dim, 1),
                nn.Sigmoid()
            ])
        
        # Projection (1x1 conv)
        layers.extend([
            nn.Conv2d(hidden_dim, C_out, 1, bias=False),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(C_out)
        ])
        
        return nn.Sequential(*layers)
    
    def search_mobile_architecture(self, train_loader, val_loader, n_trials=20):
        """Random search with latency constraint"""
        best_fitness = -float('inf')
        best_model = None
        best_stats = None
        
        for trial in range(n_trials):
            print(f"\nTrial {trial+1}/{n_trials}:")
            
            # Sample architecture: [n_blocks, expansion_rates, use_se]
            n_blocks = random.randint(4, 8)
            expansions = [random.choice([2, 4, 6]) for _ in range(n_blocks)]
            use_se = [random.choice([True, False]) for _ in range(n_blocks)]
            
            # Build model
            layers = [nn.Conv2d(3, 32, 3, padding=1)]  # Stem
            C = 32
            for exp, se in zip(expansions, use_se):
                layers.append(self.efficient_block(C, C, expansion=exp, use_se=se))
            layers.extend([nn.AdaptiveAvgPool2d(1), nn.Flatten(), nn.Linear(C, 10)])
            model = nn.Sequential(*layers)
            
            # Train briefly
            optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=0.001)
            model.train()
            for epoch in range(3):  # Quick proxy training
                for X, y in train_loader:
                    optimizer.zero_grad()
                    nn.functional.cross_entropy(model(X), y).backward()
                    optimizer.step()
            
            # Evaluate multi-objective fitness
            fitness, acc, lat = self.multi_objective_fitness(model, val_loader, input_size=(1, 3, 32, 32))
            
            if fitness > best_fitness:
                best_fitness = fitness
                best_model = model
                best_stats = (acc, lat)
                print(f"  ✅ New best! (Accuracy: {acc:.2%}, Latency: {lat:.1f}ms)")
        
        return best_model, best_stats

# Hardware-aware NAS for mobile deployment
nas = HardwareAwareNAS(target_latency_ms=50, lambda_latency=0.05)
best_model, (accuracy, latency) = nas.search_mobile_architecture(train_loader, val_loader, n_trials=30)

print(f"\n🎯 Final Architecture:")
print(f"  Validation Accuracy: {accuracy:.2%}")
print(f"  Inference Latency: {latency:.1f}ms (target: {nas.target_latency*1000}ms)")
print(f"  Ready for mobile deployment (TFLite, CoreML)!")
codeExamples.explanation: Hardware-Aware NAS: Accuracy'ye ek olarak latency, memory, energy optimize et (mobile, edge critical). Multi-objective optimization: Fitness = Acc - λ·max(0, Latency - Target). Efficient architectures: MobileNetV2/V3 (depthwise separable conv, inverted residual), EfficientNet (compound scaling). Production: TFLite benchmarking on actual device (Pixel, iPhone), Pareto frontier (multiple λ values → tradeoff curve). Real: ProxylessNAS (Google), FBNet (Facebook), Once-for-All (MIT). Deploy: TFLite, CoreML, ONNX Runtime.
